text.tspan: Amazon EKS: node types and data volumes
• EKS creates and manages the nodes
• Nodes are part of an ASG
to the cluster, in your own ASG
• Mix any of these in one
EKS data volumes: StorageClass + CSI driver
Course list: EBS, EFS (works with Fargate), FSx for Lustre, FSx for NetApp ONTAP.
Docs add: FSx for OpenZFS, Amazon File Cache, Mountpoint for Amazon S3, S3 Files (through the EFS CSI driver, not on Fargate), instance store.
EBS = one AZ, one node (ReadWriteOnce) · EFS = many pods across AZs (ReadWriteMany) · Fargate pods: EFS only, no EBS.
Also: one EKS cluster per Region for multi-Region; logs and metrics with CloudWatch Container Insights.
• "Already use Kubernetes on-prem or in another cloud, move to AWS" → EKS (Kubernetes is cloud-agnostic). Otherwise ECS is simpler.
• "Least node management on EKS" → Fargate (or Auto Mode). "Spot nodes managed for me" → managed node group with Spot capacity type.
• "Shared storage for pods in several AZs" → EFS CSI driver. "Fast block storage for one pod" → EBS CSI driver.
